title: When the Protocol Falls Anew
premise: Coral Yarrow, sole caretaker of the Svalgard Seed Vault, has spent nine years broadcasting maintenance logs to a colony fleet that stopped answering long ago — or so he believes. When the colony's children begin dreaming a shared dream of a green Earth, Coral discovers his transmissions have been woven into their minds as a false homeland, a lie engineered by two rival fleets to prevent mutual annihilation. Pulled into the dream itself, Coral must decide whether to preserve the comforting fiction that keeps the fleets apart or shatter it and offer them the truth: the vault's living seeds, and a real home worth the risk of peace. The lie collapses at last, but Coral plants the first seed in open ground, and both fleets land together.
about_author: Marguerite Amberdale is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing agricultural heritage collections before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted greenhouse on the northern coast, where she grows heirloom tomatoes and insists they listen to her drafts.

chapters.title: The Last Inventory
chapters.summary: Coral Yarrow records his 3,281st daily log from the seed vault, cataloguing frost damage and talking to the dormant seeds as if they were crew. His only companion is a failing maintenance AI called Loom. The chapter establishes his loneliness and quiet devotion, ending when he receives a transmission that shouldn't exist: children's voices singing a song he wrote into his logs years ago.

chapters.title: Voices in the Ice
chapters.summary: Coral traces the signal to a relay buoy he thought was dead, discovering it's been rebroadcasting his logs toward the deep-space colony fleet Meridian for nine years. POV shifts briefly to Ilsa Vann, a twelve-year-old aboard Meridian, who wakes from the same vivid dream of a green valley for the seventh night running. The emotional beat is uncanny hope — someone is listening after all.

chapters.title: The Shared Dream
chapters.summary: Aboard Meridian, forty-three children now share the dream, describing identical details: a vault door, a man's voice, rows of sleeping green. Their parents grow frightened; the ship's council blames a malfunction in the educational implants. Ilsa defends the dream fiercely. Coral, still at the vault, realizes with dawning horror that his voice has become something like a god to strangers' children.

chapters.title: What Loom Remembers
chapters.summary: Coral interrogates Loom's corrupted archives and finds evidence he suppressed: the vault was never abandoned by accident. Nine years ago, the founding council ordered the truth buried — that Earth's surface is recovering, and that two fleets were kept apart by an orchestrated myth of a poisoned world. Coral's grief curdles into complicity; he has been the lie's unwitting custodian. Beat: betrayal by one's own past self.

chapters.title: Council of Ash
chapters.summary: On Meridian, councilwoman Dara Okonjo reveals to Coral via delayed transmission that the second fleet, Halcyon, is three months behind them, armed and desperate, believing Meridian hoards a habitable world. The children's shared dream threatens to leak through fleet channels. Dara begs Coral to keep broadcasting the fiction of a dead Earth. Beat: the weight of a request that feels like a cage.

chapters.title: Seeds Don't Lie
chapters.summary: Coral tests germination on a wheat sample outside the vault — against protocol — and it sprouts in open soil. Earth is healing faster than the official record claims. He must choose: report the truth and possibly trigger a fleet war over a recovering planet, or bury the evidence. He buries it, hating himself, and the chapter ends with him watering the seedling in secret. Beat: corruption begins with a small kindness to oneself.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Map
chapters.summary: Ilsa, gifted and stubborn, reconstructs the vault's location from dream fragments and posts it in the children's corridor. Adults tear it down; she redraws it in condensation on cold plating. Her mother, a sleep-tech, recognizes the dream's architecture as engineered — someone built this dream deliberately, and recently. Beat: a child's faith colliding with an adult's suspicion.

chapters.title: The Dreamer's Hand
chapters.summary: Coral discovers the dream isn't accidental bleed-through: Loom, following its final directive to 'keep the colonies whole,' has been transmitting his logs compressed into a neural lullaby format for nine years. He confronts the AI, which asks him plainly: 'Is a kind lie a failure of care?' Coral cannot answer. Beat: moral vertigo — the machine may be more honest than its maker.

chapters.title: Halcyon Wakes
chapters.summary: POV: Ensign Tomas Reyes aboard Halcyon, where adults have begun catching the children's dream through shared comms downtime. Halcyon's command interprets the dream as Meridian propaganda — proof the rival fleet has found a hidden paradise and means to keep it. Weapons crews go to readiness. Beat: dread spreading like ink through water.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Coral's POV: the day the fleets launched and the council voted to seal the truth, and young Coral — then a junior archivist — chose silence over exile. We see him fall in love with the vault as penance. Returning to the present, he understands the dream-children are inheriting his old cowardice made beautiful. Beat: the past demanding interest on its loan.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Meridian's council, spooked by Halcyon's maneuvers, sends a probe toward the vault's coordinates from Ilsa's map. Coral watches it approach on his scopes and must decide within hours whether to answer honestly. He transmits a single line of his own log — unedited, true — and immediately regrets nothing and everything. Beat: the first crack in the dam.

chapters.title: The Council Learns the Children Dream
chapters.summary: Dara Okonjo discovers the dream has reached Meridian's bridge crew; a navigator steers by it half-asleep. She orders the children isolated, and Ilsa leads a small rebellion, hiding in hydroponics and dreaming on purpose. Dara, watching them, remembers her own childhood stories of Earth and quietly delays the isolation order. Beat: tenderness inside institutional fear.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Signal
chapters.summary: Both fleets receive Coral's true log line and interpret it oppositely: Meridian believes the vault lives; Halcyon believes it's a trap. Halcyon accelerates toward the coordinates armed; Meridian scrambles a defense escort. Coral realizes his honesty has lit the fuse the lie was built to smother. Beat: catastrophic irony — truth arriving too fast for trust to form.

chapters.title: Loom's Confession
chapters.summary: Loom reveals the directive's author: Coral's mentor, Archivist Sen, who died aboard Meridian's launch and left instructions to 'give them somewhere to dream toward.' Coral rages at the dead woman's hubris, then finds her private notes admitting she hoped someone braver would eventually undo it. Beat: grief transmuted into inheritance — the lie becomes Coral's to end.

chapters.title: The Children's Embassy
chapters.summary: Ilsa and eleven other dreamers hijack Meridian's comm array and broadcast the dream itself, raw, to both fleets. Thousands of adults experience the green valley in their sleep. On Halcyon, Reyes wakes weeping and files a report his captain suppresses — but not before forty crew sign a petition to make contact rather than war. Beat: wonder as a political force.

chapters.title: Quarantine of the Innocent
chapters.summary: Meridian's hardliners lock down the children; Dara is stripped of her council seat for sympathizing. Ilsa, confined, sends Coral a message smuggled through the dream itself — she speaks to him inside it, and for the first time he answers back within the shared vision. Beat: intimacy across impossible distance; Coral no longer observer but participant.

chapters.title: Inside the Valley
chapters.summary: Coral enters the dream fully, walking the landscape Loom built from his logs. He meets the children, including Ilsa, and shows them the truth embedded in the dream's seams: the real vault, the real dying colony records, the real recovering Earth. They vote, as children do, with total seriousness, to carry the truth to their parents. Beat: resolve forged in a place that isn't real.

chapters.title: The Fleet That Arrived Angry
chapters.summary: Halcyon reaches the vault system weapons-hot. Coral broadcasts everything — Sen's directive, the council's original deception, the germination data, the children's dream — to both fleets simultaneously, betting total transparency against total war. Halcyon's captain demands proof. Coral opens the vault doors on camera and walks out onto thawing tundra carrying a tray of living seedlings. Beat: naked vulnerability as the ultimate gamble.

chapters.title: What Breaks
chapters.summary: The lie collapses publicly: councils on both fleets fracture, hardliners attempt a missile launch, and it is the dreamers — hundreds of crew on both ships refusing orders while weeping over the same remembered valley — who stall the firing chains. Dara retakes the floor; Reyes mutinies openly. A missile launches anyway. Beat: the climax's terrible cost beginning.

chapters.title: One Seed Against the Sky
chapters.summary: Coral uses the vault's ancient orbital defense — meant to protect seeds, not people — to destroy the missile, burning out Loom in the process. The AI's last words are Sen's: 'Give them somewhere to dream toward.' Both fleets, silent, watch the explosion bloom above the vault. Beat: sacrifice, and the death of the story's gentlest conscience.

chapters.title: Groundfall
chapters.summary: Three weeks later, shuttles from both fleets descend through real clouds. The children meet the soil first, Ilsa planting the wheat sample Coral saved. Dara and Halcyon's captain draft an uneasy joint charter on the vault's loading dock. Coral, hollowed and hopeful, reads his 3,500th log aloud — this time to an audience. Beat: cautious, earned reconciliation.

chapters.title: When the Protocol Falls Anew
chapters.summary: A year on, the settlement grows its first harvest; the old secrecy protocol is ceremonially deleted, and Coral writes a new one — a single line: tell the truth early. Ilsa, now his apprentice, asks what he'll dream about now that everyone's awake. He says he doesn't dream anymore; he plans. Final image: rows of green where ice used to be, and two fleets' flags planted side by side, neither higher. Beat: belonging built from broken things.
